summary: Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander C. Soper and studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda, later serving as professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid works in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu, where she is attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa under Nalini Devdas and served as assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities (attested 2008).

Angela Zito works in religious studies and Sinology. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1979–1989) and became associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University around 1998, also co-founding positions: asia critique.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs completed her PhD at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1985–1993) under Bernard Williams. She was an assistant professor at Frankfurt (1993–2001) and was appointed to the chair of practical philosophy at the University of Basel in 2001.

Angelika Malinar is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who completed her PhD (1985–1991) and Habilitation (1991–1998) at the University of Tübingen. She taught at SOAS (~2000–2007) before becoming professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.

Angelo de Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Florence (1863–1891) and Sanskrit and Italian literature at Rome (1890).

Anil Vidyalankar (b. 1928) is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (Ph.D.), and founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its director (attested 1999).

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and The University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud, 2009), and held an attested post at the University of Delhi in 2012.

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her Master of Arts at the Australian National University under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus (attested 1983).
Ann Gleig is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold (b. 1946) specializes in Indology and religious studies. After completing her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1973–1984), she held posts at Cornell (~1986–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993–2021).

Ann Heirman (b. 1965) specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and at Ghent University, where she became professor of Chinese language and culture and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2002).

Ann Laura Stoler (b. 1949) studied at Barnard College and Columbia University. She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and the University of Michigan (1989–2004), before chairing the anthropology department at The New School in 2004.

Anna Aurelia Esposito specializes in Indology. She studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Tübingen (MA, 1998), and held an assistant professorship to the Chair of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, also studying under traditional teachers, and became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology in 2002.

Anna Brown works in religious studies and political science. She studied Zen under Robert Kennedy and served at Saint Peter's University as chair of the political science department and director of the social justice program (attested 2017).

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and lectured at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields (b. 1966) is a Sinologist. She held faculty posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and at Princeton University (~2015).
Anna Madelyn Hennessey is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara under the supervision of William F. Powell (attested 2011).
